title: Normalized CE cohomology on individual filtered cycle representatives
statement: For every scheme $X$ and bounded-below integer cochain complex $K$ of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], prescribe an augmented bicomplex $a(X,K):K\to I(X,K)$ with complex degrees in $\mathbb Z$ and resolution degrees in $\mathbb N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Assume individual lower bounds in complex degree, injectivity of all terms and all horizontal cycle, boundary and homology terms, and quasi-isomorphisms on augmented rows and on their horizontal cycle, boundary and homology complexes. There exist simultaneous presentations P, positive-page representative differentials delta and comparison isomorphisms j retaining the prescribed I and normalized successor homology comparisons. For each scheme map f, coefficient-complex map v, augmented row comparison phi and diagonal-compatible sheaf-total map u, let b be the conjugated sections lift. Given any test object A, degree p in N, degree q in Z, filtered representatives x,y and graded cycle maps z,z' whose equations identify y with bx and z,z' with their graded projections, the source quotient class composed with j inverse, firstPageIso and Sheaf.H.map(v^q,p) after cohomologyMap(f,K^q,p) equals the target quotient class composed with j inverse and firstPageIso. No filtration-restriction hypothesis and no supplied first-page map M occur; this is only the local representative calculation.

proof.text: Obtain P, delta, j, the signed row isomorphisms e, retention of I and normalized successors, and the first-page-to-row comparison equation from the normalized row representative construction.

For the augmented row map phi.f q apply the ordinary row cohomology naturality theorem to cePresentationRow of the two presentations and the coefficient map v.f q. Rewrite the source and target first-page comparisons as e followed by ceRowOrdinaryIso. The row naturality square replaces the ordinary cohomology map with row homology followed by the target comparison. Postcompose the row representative equality by that comparison. Associativity then gives exactly the stated local equality.
